Thanks for the call this morning, Jonas. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can finish the evaluation:

- Our hypothetical traffic profile is bursty: 60 concurrent requests at peak, average prompt length ~450 tokens, generation length ~200 tokens.

Can you share any existing numbers you have for Redwood vs hyperscaler managed endpoints (p95, p99, tokens/sec) for comparably-sized models and the test harness you used? If possible, drop your raw bench outputs and any sample payloads so we can run a quick smoke A/B on our side.

Date: 2027-06-21 11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery call — latency / throughput ask

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Bringing a quick, pragmatic recap plus the attachments we discussed: redwood_prelim_bench_20270621.pdf (summary) and sample_payloads.json (example requests). Key highlights from our internal microbench (representative setup: A100-like instance pool, 8 GPUs, 512 batch pad profile):

- p95 latency (1k context, 650 tokens total): 210 ms (Redwood hosted API single-region, steady-state)
- p99 latency (same workload): 410 ms
- Sustained tokens/sec (aggregate across pool): ~37k tokens/sec for the workload shape described
- Notes: Our test used continuous batching with prefix/KV cache for repeated system prompts; we also measured cold-start single-request p95 ~480 ms.

How this compares vs typical hyperscaler endpoints (summary):
- Hyperscaler A (managed endpoint): p95 ~360 ms, p99 ~780 ms, tokens/sec ~22k (observed in our internal head-to-head where we matched model family and input sizing)
- Hyperscaler B (serverless-style): variable — better for single-request median, worse for steady throughput due to throttling; p95 ~420 ms in our runs.

Caveats: direct comparisons depend heavily on instance types, concurrency shaping, and whether a provider exposes steady reserved capacity vs ephemeral. The attached PDF has raw numbers, test harness command lines, and the exact model variants/quantization settings we used.

Proposed next step: authorize a short A/B run where we and you run the same sample_payloads.json against Redwood hosted (or a dedicated trial) and one hyperscaler endpoint you want to compare. We can coordinate a 2-hour window and capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and CPU/GPU utilization traces.

Action items: 
- Alex: confirm the hyperscaler target (A or B or specific endpoint) and available 2-hour windows next week
- Lauren: prepare a one-click test run (will send link) and flag any compliance artifacts needed for procurement

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
